context:
Fetch the WDC Training Dataset and Gold Standard for Large-Scale Product Matching, version 2 (Primpeli, Peeters and Bizer, 2019), the hand-checked gold standard file of 4,398 product-offer pairs published by the Web Data Commons project at the University of Mannheim:

https://data.dws.informatik.uni-mannheim.de/largescaleproductcorpus/data/v2_nonnorm/goldstandards/all_gs.json.gz

If that host is unreachable after a few tries, the Internet Archive's capture of the same file from 2022-07-12 serves identical bytes at https://web.archive.org/web/20220712201723id_/http://data.dws.informatik.uni-mannheim.de/largescaleproductcorpus/data/v2_nonnorm/goldstandards/all_gs.json.gz. Either way, the downloaded bytes must have SHA-256 4adf972cc973e7ce12ab819a682b66f98708e29fa4a088aca11726a0cbd65c1b.

The file is a gzip-compressed JSON Lines document: each line is one pair of offers from two different web shops. Each object has pair_id (the two offers' ids joined by '#'), label ('1' means the pair was hand-checked as the same product, '0' as different), and, with _left and _right suffixes, the fields title, brand, price and description. Before reading the texts, clean them: remove the schema.org language tags ('"@en', '"@en-us'), remove stray double quotes, and collapse runs of whitespace. Use at most the first 300 characters of each description.

The ten pairs of a batch are fixed by the data alone and no pair is used twice. Order the label-1 pairs by the SHA-256 hex digest of their pair_id (UTF-8) and order the label-0 pairs the same way. Batch k takes the next 2 + (k mod 3) label-1 pairs and the next 8 - (k mod 3) label-0 pairs, sorts those 10 selected pairs by the SHA-256 hex digest of their pair_id again, and numbers them p01 to p10 in that order.

For each pair, decide whether the two offers sell the same manufacturer product: the same model, and the same part or style number where the offers give one. The shops word and translate titles differently, add a lens or memory card they bundle, and name colors in their own words; none of that makes it a different product. A different model or version (often one digit or letter apart, like D5300 and D5500), or an accessory sold on its own, is a different product. The similarity of the two titles is only a hint: very similar titles can name different models, and very different titles can be the same product. Decide from the model, part and style numbers in the titles, brands and descriptions; the label column only fixes which pairs form the batch, so the decision itself must come from the offers' texts.

Output one JSON object with the batch number as given and exactly the keys p01_p04, p05_p07 and p08_p10. Each of those three keys holds an object with a single key "same", whose value is the array of the slots in that group whose two offers are the same product, or an empty array when none is. In total the three "same" arrays together must list exactly 2 + batch mod 3 slots.
